title: Canadian national arrested at Katunayake Airport with hashish worth over Rs. 200 Mn
byline: A 27-year-old Canadian national has been arrested at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in Katunayake after airport officials discovered hashish worth over Rs. 200 million concealed in his luggage.

title: Vehicle mows down crowd at Berlin Pride festival, killing one
byline: One person has been killed and 17 injured, ​with some in life-threatening condition, after a vehicle mowed down a crowd near Berlin’s Pride celebrations on Saturday evening, setting off a ‌manhunt for those responsible, the police said.

title: Teachers’ Union slams compulsory Poya Day meeting for principals
byline: The Ceylon Teachers’ Union (CTU) has strongly condemned the decision to hold a meeting for school principals in the Kandy education zone on a Poya Day (29), with General Secretary Joseph Stalin accusing education authorities of making an unfair decision on behalf of the government.

title: Baghaei says progress made in Oman talks on Strait of Hormuz
byline: Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei says talks were held with Oman on Friday and Saturday over shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. He said progress has been made.

title: National drowning prevention committee to be formed
byline: The Government has taken steps to establish a multi-stakeholder national mechanism for drowning prevention and lifesaving, with a progress review meeting held at the Parliament Complex to strengthen coordination among key agencies.

title: Hotel in Ella fined Rs. 1 Mn for overpricing bottled water
byline: The Bandarawela Magistrate’s Court has imposed a Rs. 1 million fine on a hotel in the Nafora area of Karandagolla, Ella, after it admitted to selling bottled drinking water above the stipulated maximum retail price, authorities said.

title: Police Inspector arrested for alleged drunk driving after two hit-and-run crashes
byline: A Chief Inspector of Police attached to the Special Investigation Unit of the Homagama Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Division has been arrested for allegedly driving under the influence of alcohol and fleeing the scene after striking two young women in two separate road accidents, police said.

title: Sub-Inspector suspended over misconduct and aggressive behavior
byline: A Sub-Inspector attached to the Wathupitiwala Investment Zone Police Post has been suspended with immediate effect following an incident involving inappropriate conduct and threatening behavior toward members of the public.

title: Rescuers scour South China Sea for 23 missing after Vietnamese vessel sinks
byline: Rescuers were searching on Sunday for 23 people missing after a Vietnamese ship ​sank in the busy waterway of the ‌South China Sea, while 39 were pulled from the waters, China’s state broadcaster CCTV said.

title: Two arrested over Bellanwila shooting
byline: Two suspects have been arrested in connection with the fatal shooting of a man in Bellanwila, Boralesgamuwa last night.

title: Over 1,000 uncleared vehicles at Hambantota Port to face Customs auction
byline: Sri Lanka Customs is preparing to auction or sell more than 1,000 imported vehicles that have remained uncleared at the Hambantota Port, officials said.

title: Dengue death toll rises to 61 as cases surpass 81,500
byline: Sri Lanka’s dengue death toll has risen to 61 this year, while the total number of reported cases has increased to 81,511, according to the latest data released by the National Dengue Control Unit (NDCU).

title: Sarnath joins Unesco World Heritage list
byline: India’s ancient Buddhist site of Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh was on Saturday inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, becoming India’s 45th site to receive this recognition. India ranks sixth globally and second in Asia Pacific Region for the most number of ‘World Heritage Sites’.

title: Pralhad Joshi appointed Union Education Minister
byline: Pralhad Joshi was appointed as the new Union Education Minister on Saturday (July 25, 2026) after the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhanfollowing nationwide protests.

title: Police recommend removing Kavadi dance from Devinuwara Perahera over security concerns
byline: Police have recommended removing the traditional Kavadi dance performance from the upcoming procession of the historic Sri Utpalawanna Sri Vishnu Maha Devalaya in Devinuwara, citing security concerns.

title: Iran war spreads to Red Sea and Caspian, Gulf quiet as US forgoes strikes
byline: The Iran war ​broadened over the weekend despite a pause in U.S. strikes, as Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis attacked Saudi oil installations along the Red Sea coast and Iran ‌accused Ukraine of targeting one of its vessels in the Caspian Sea.

title: Rainfall expected to increase in southwest from July 28: Met Dept
byline: The Meteorology Department has forecast a slight increase in rainfall in the south-western parts of Sri Lanka over the next few days from July 28.

title: No closure of Sri Vijaya Dhamma School in Saudi Arabia
byline: A clarification has been issued rejecting claims that the Sri Vijaya Buddhist Dhamma School in Riyadh was closed on the instructions of Sri Lanka’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Amir Ajwad, describing the reports as false and based on distorted information.

title: Trump pauses Iran strikes over missile shortages
byline: Donald Trump has paused plans to escalate the war on Iran after being warned that the US is running low on missiles.

title: Referendum needed on Supreme Court judges’ tenure: Namal
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser and MP Namal Rajapaksa said any proposal to extend the tenure of Supreme Court judges should be decided by the people through a referendum.

title: Former Envoy Kananathan salutes Liberia on 179th Independence Day, signals renewable energy partnership initiative
byline: Former Envoy Ambassador Kananathan has extended his warmest congratulations today to His Excellency President Joseph Nyuma Boakai,  the Government, and the people of the Republic of Liberia on the occasion of the country’s 179th Independence Day.

title: Shan Althaf’s Trinity immortals of 2026
byline: Inter-school rugby season 2026 scripted a story of unmatched quality produced by Trinity College Kandy culminating with the second leg of the 80th Bradby Shield encounter on the 25th of July at the Lion’s Den at picturesque Pallekele Rugby Stadium.
